exposure: New York Heart Association functional class III~IV
No congenital heart disease surgery prior to pregnancy
cohort: The study included 19,424 deliveries at Beijing Anzhen Hospital between 2010 and 2019, comparing women with and without congenital heart disease.
finding: Women with congenital heart disease have increased maternal and infant risks during pregnancy and the perinatal period, including higher rates of maternal death, longer hospital stays, pre-term delivery, heart failure, arrhythmia, and infants with low birth weight or CHD.
mod_finding: Cesarean section was identified as an adverse event associated with pulmonary hypertension, decreased cardiac function, and no previous CHD surgery in women with congenital heart disease.
